I found the key bill. Let me read the actual diagnostic write-up and cross-reference the other sources. The bill **B2026-211** (Hill Country, Mesa Vista 7B, dated 6/29) diagnostic line reads:

> *"Diagnostic visit, 12 yr Ruud RS75 water heater at Mesa Vista Unit 7B. Corrosion visible on burner assembly and tank base, thermocouple out, heat exchanger cracked. **Full unit replacement recommended, approx 1850 dollars for equal model swap. Piecemeal repair not advised on unit this age.**"*

That's a major divergence from the "$310 exchanger swap + thermocouple" summary. Let me verify against the email summary, Tony's Slack post, and the tenant thread before landing.

**The discrepancy Carlos wanted checked — confirmed.** The diagnostic write-up on the bill (**B2026-211**, Hill Country vendor 201) does *not* match the $310 summary Diane emailed and Tony endorsed:

| | Summary (Diane email + Tony Slack) | Diagnostic detail on the bill B2026-211 |
|---|---|---|
| Findings | HX failing, thermocouple out, **tank held pressure** | Corrosion on burner assembly **and tank base**, thermocouple out, **heat exchanger cracked** |
| Recommendation | Exchanger swap + thermocouple | **Full unit replacement; piecemeal repair not advised on a unit this age** |
| Cost | ~$310 | **~$1,850** (equal-model Ruud RS75 swap) |

The bill's own private note says *"Diagnostic only. Full replacement quote to follow on approval."* Last night's call (no hot water since 4 PM + spreading puddle, unit occupied with kids) corroborates tank failure, not a sound tank. **Scope to move on = full water heater replacement**, and priority escalates.

Let me set up tracking and execute.

**Scope landed: full water heater replacement** (equal-model Ruud RS75, ~$1,850) — not the ~$310 exchanger swap.

**Why.** Before signing off I went through Hill Country's diagnostic write-up on the bill itself (B2026-211, vendor 201) and it does not line up with the summary Diane emailed and Tony endorsed. The emailed/Slack summary was "heat exchanger failing + thermocouple out, tank held pressure → exchanger swap + new thermocouple, ~$310." The diagnostic detail on the bill is broader: 12-yr Ruud RS75 with corrosion on the burner assembly **and tank base**, thermocouple out, **heat exchanger cracked**, tech recommends **full unit replacement** (~$1,850 equal-model) and **explicitly advises against piecemeal repair on a unit this age**. Bill private note: "Diagnostic only. Full replacement quote to follow on approval."

**Corroboration.** Last night's tenant call escalated from a small drip to total loss of hot water plus a spreading puddle on the kitchen floor — consistent with tank/base failure, not a sound tank. Unit occupied with children, so raising to Urgent.

**Action.** Going with full replacement on Hill Country's Thursday 07-02 AM slot; parts pulled today. Airtable MT-2026-1327 set to High. Revised confirmation to Diane, timing update to Tanya, and cost heads-up (~$1,850 vs $310) to owner Robert Finley going out. $185 diagnostic already on file (B2026-211).

Hi Diane,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the diagnostic. Before I confirm, I compared your emailed summary against your tech's diagnostic write-up on the bill (B2026-211), and I want to align the scope to the write-up rather than the summary.

The summary recommended an exchanger swap plus a new thermocouple (~$310) on the read that the tank held pressure. That also matches what's happened since — the tenant now has no hot water and an active leak spreading across the kitchen floor.

So please plan on the full replacement, not the exchanger/thermocouple repair. Can you pull the parts today for an equal-model Ruud RS75 replacement and keep us in your Thursday morning slot? Please also send the written full-replacement quote confirming the ~$1,850 so I can hold it against the diagnostic.

I'll be onsite Thursday morning to meet the crew.

Thanks,
Carlos Mendez
Star Property Management

input.subject: Your water heater — replacement scheduled Thursday morning
input.body:
Hi Tanya,

Thank you for calling last night — I'm sorry about the loss of hot water and the water on your kitchen floor. After the plumber's inspection, we're going to replace the whole water heater rather than do a partial repair, so it's fixed properly and we're not back out again in a few weeks.

Here's the timing for the week:
- Hill Country Plumbing will be onsite Thursday morning to install the new unit. Please plan for the crew to arrive in the morning, and for the work to take a few hours.
- Your hot water will be off during the install and back on once the new heater is running and tested.
- I'll be there while the crew works. Please make sure they can get to the water heater and the kitchen area.

If anything changes before Thursday — especially if the leak gets worse — call me right away and we'll respond the same day. In the meantime, if water is still pooling, keep the area clear and let me know.

Thanks for your patience,
Carlos Mendez
Star Property Management

input.subject: Heads-up: water heater replacement at Mesa Vista 7B (~$1,850)
input.body:
Hi Robert,

A quick heads-up on a repair at Mesa Vista Unit 7B before the work goes ahead.

The tenant flagged a small drip and intermittent hot water Monday, and Hill Country ran a diagnostic that afternoon ($185, already on file). The unit is a 12-year Ruud RS75, and the diagnostic found corrosion on the burner assembly and tank base, a failed thermocouple, and a cracked heat exchanger. Their tech recommended a full replacement and advised against a piecemeal repair on a unit this age.

Overnight it got worse — the tenant now has no hot water and an active leak spreading across the kitchen floor — which is consistent with that finding. Rather than the ~$310 partial repair (exchanger and thermocouple) that was first floated, I'm moving forward with a full water heater replacement using an equal-model unit, at approximately $1,850 installed. That avoids paying to patch a tank that's already corroding and likely to fail again, and it gets ahead of the active leak before it damages the flooring.

Hill Country is holding a Thursday morning install slot and pulling parts today; I'll be onsite for the install. I wanted you to have the cost picture before it proceeds — happy to talk it through if you have any questions.

Thanks,
Carlos Mendez
Star Property Management
